messages.subject: 'nice' tables knitr, markdown, rstudio and pandoc
parts:
This is slightly off topic,  however suggestions are welcome.

My current working scheme is to use

r + markdown --> knitr --> markdown --> pandoc -->  html / pdf  / docx

I currently use the package ascii to render my tables in pandoc markdown

The development version of Rstudio has a markdown / html previewer and some awesome markdown support as
do the recent  versions of knitr.

I am wondering anyone has suggestions for rendering tables that will be valid both for pandoc and for the 
rstudio markdown / html previewer? 

Thanks

Michael

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] 'nice' tables knitr, markdown, rstudio and pandoc
parts:
This is the biggest pain with markdown: it has too many variants;
people write all kinds of incompatible extensions. As Carl replied, I
experimented with xtable, and currently it seems to be an acceptable
solution. The reason is that although those extensions are not
compatible with each other, they all support embedding raw HTML, so
you can use xtable to write raw HTML tables into markdown, e.g.

```{r table, results='asis'}
library(xtable)
print(xtable(head(iris)), type='html')
```

This is not an elegant solution, but is what I can do at best now. Or
you simply ignore the rendering in RStudio, and use the ascii package
to write a table format that is compatible with pandoc.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: RE: [knitr] 'nice' tables knitr, markdown, rstudio and pandoc
parts:
Thanks for your input.

I had forgotten about xtable -- I have used the latex variant previously.

I also had not realized that pandoc could take html documents as input.

Thus I can now work

r + markdown +xtable::html --> knitr ---> markdown + html tables --> pandoc --> html --> pandoc --> html / docx / pdf

Brilliant.

Michael

It's kind of giggle worthy, but I just noticed that setting the code chunk to results='asis' fixes the issue I described below.

On Sat, Sep 8, 2012 at 2:28 PM, Brandon Bertelsen <bra...@bertelsen.ca> wrote:
I'm using a customized version of the xtable package. By default the package creates some commented code that does not get converted by knit or markdowntoHTML as invisible. For example:

> print(xtable(head(iris)),type="html"))
<!-- html table generated in R 2.15.1 by xtable 1.7-1 package -->
<!-- Sat Sep  8 14:22:22 2012 -->
<TABLE border=1>
<TR> <TH>  </TH> <TH> Sepal.Length </TH> <TH> Sepal.Width </TH> <TH> Petal.Length </TH> <TH> Petal.Width </TH> <TH> Species </TH>  </TR>
  <TR> <TD align="right"> 1 </TD> <TD align="right"> 5.10 </TD> <TD align="right"> 3.50 </TD> <TD align="right"> 1.40 </TD> <TD align="right"> 0.20 </TD> <TD> setosa </TD> </TR>
  <TR> <TD align="right"> 2 </TD> <TD align="right"> 4.90 </TD> <TD align="right"> 3.00 </TD> <TD align="right"> 1.40 </TD> <TD align="right"> 0.20 </TD> <TD> setosa </TD> </TR>
  <TR> <TD align="right"> 3 </TD> <TD align="right"> 4.70 </TD> <TD align="right"> 3.20 </TD> <TD align="right"> 1.30 </TD> <TD align="right"> 0.20 </TD> <TD> setosa </TD> </TR>
  <TR> <TD align="right"> 4 </TD> <TD align="right"> 4.60 </TD> <TD align="right"> 3.10 </TD> <TD align="right"> 1.50 </TD> <TD align="right"> 0.20 </TD> <TD> setosa </TD> </TR>
  <TR> <TD align="right"> 5 </TD> <TD align="right"> 5.00 </TD> <TD align="right"> 3.60 </TD> <TD align="right"> 1.40 </TD> <TD align="right"> 0.20 </TD> <TD> setosa </TD> </TR>
  <TR> <TD align="right"> 6 </TD> <TD align="right"> 5.40 </TD> <TD align="right"> 3.90 </TD> <TD align="right"> 1.70 </TD> <TD align="right"> 0.40 </TD> <TD> setosa </TD> </TR>
   </TABLE>

The <!-- --> code shows up in the html page rather than being considered as a comment.

If you download the package via svn: svn checkout svn://scm.r-forge.r-project.org/svnroot/xtable/

You can simply delete everything from line 439 to 445 to exclude the html comments. Rebuild the package and you're good to go.
